channel.title: Battery Sensei
channel.description: Updates for Battery Sensei — a quiet macOS menu-bar battery utility.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
1.0

Battery Sensei is the menu-bar battery utility I wanted but couldn't find. One that knows my calendar.

It reads your next four hours of meetings and warns you before your battery dies during one. At -30, -15, -5, or -1 minutes. You pick. Event titles never leave your Mac.

It also does the usual: charge cap with weekly recalibration, per-app battery use over the last hour / day / week, and a soft history strip so you can see what your battery has been through.

Five languages. macOS 14 or later. Apple Silicon or Intel.

Drag it into Applications.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
1.1

Sharper meeting alerts and a real Settings window.

You now pick exactly which checkpoints fire before each meeting: -30, -15, -5, -1. Default is -30 and -5. The toggle chips match the website. Changes apply the moment you flip them.

The Settings window stops vanishing when you click another app. (It used to. Sorry.)

Other small things:

  • "Latest forecast" stays put when no meeting needs warning about. Empty state reads "No conflicts" instead of disappearing.
  • Hover states on snooze buttons and reminder chips, finally.
  • "Show event titles" replaces "Hide event titles". Default is on.
  • Live "N min left" countdown actually counts down now.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
1.1.1

Sparkle now downloads and installs updates silently. You won't see another "Install update?" prompt unless you opt out in the dialog.

Two layout fixes: the Activate Pro button matches the Buy button's height again, and the Latest forecast card aligns to one column instead of three.

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
1.2

One-click activation after you buy.

Click "Open Sensei & activate" on the thank-you page and the app opens with your license key already typed in. You click Activate. That's it. No more copy-paste from the email.

Also: the in-app Buy button now drops you straight into the checkout flow instead of bouncing through the marketing page.

item.title: Version 1.2.1
item.description:
1.2.1

Two reliability fixes.

The "Install and Relaunch" window now actually comes to the front when Sparkle has an update ready. Previously the app was a menu-bar accessory and the prompt could be born behind whatever you were doing.

Activating a new license no longer risks leaving you locked out. The new key gets activated first; the old one only releases if the new one succeeds. Network blip, typo, cancelled mid-flow — your existing license stays put. The sheet now shows a small warning when you're about to swap.

item.title: Version 1.2.2
item.description:
1.2.2

Settings polish.

The settings window no longer floats above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Standard window ordering applies: click the full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

The menu-bar display picker (Percent / Time / Icon) got a once-over. All three battery glyphs are now the same width regardless of which mode you pick. The selected tile is outlined in red in light mode and white in dark mode — border only, no background fill, so the preview strip behind reads through.

Manage and Run Setup Wizard Again lost their trailing dots, along with Settings, Share image, Activate Pro, Check for Updates, and Check now. Cleaner action labels across the app.

License section: Manage Subscription is now a proper accent link with hover, matching how Manage Activations already looks in the activation sheet. Remove from this Mac stays a bordered button — destructive actions earn deliberate buttons.

Activating a different license key no longer risks locking you out. The new key is activated first; the old one only releases if that succeeds. Failed network, typo, sheet cancellation — your existing license stays put. The activation sheet shows a small warning banner when you're about to swap so you know what's happening.

item.title: Version 1.2.3
item.description:
1.2.3

Quieter idle, sharper feedback.

Battery Sensei now does noticeably less work when nothing's happening. The menu-bar charging pulse runs at half the previous rate (still reads as motion, half the redraws), the icon render cache holds 4× more entries so the percent/time display stops thrashing, and the meeting forecast only re-publishes when the predicted severity actually changes. A few CPU hot spots in the per-app history store got cleaned up too.

Hover affordances filled in across the app. Every interactive surface, including the warning-mode wizard cards, the language picker, the saga search clear button, and the rescue-receipt dismiss, now responds to pointer-over with a subtle scale lift and pointing-hand cursor. Six gaps closed.

Removing a license from this Mac now asks first. Confirmation dialog explains the slot returns to your pool, and the destructive button is clearly labeled. Hover on the button is consistent with the Manage link beside it.

The settings window stops floating above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Click a full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

A few visual fit-and-finish bits: the Lifetime badge corner radius now matches the Remove button beside it, the hero card kanji watermark lights red on hover like all the other cards, and the menu-bar icon picker has a uniform battery glyph width across Percent / Time / Icon.

item.title: Version 1.2.4
item.description:
1.2.4

Lighter idle, sharper history, calmer meeting alerts.

The per-app history store no longer blocks the main thread on every sample tick. JSON re-encodes and disk writes now run on a background queue and coalesce back-to-back saves into a single write — the sampler itself returns instantly. Top-app aggregations are memoized inside each tick so the same window query never re-runs the filter, group, and battery-attribution pass twice. A battery app shouldn't drain battery; it now drains noticeably less.

The Saga charge history chart got a hover crosshair. Scrub the line and a pinned tooltip shows the timestamp and exact percentage of the nearest sample, anchored to the chart bounds so it never clips off-screen. Tap-away clears it. The annotation snaps to real readings instead of interpolating between them.

Meeting battery alerts dropped the redundant "Meeting battery guard" kicker. The calendar hero already establishes context and the sentence already names the event, so the alert now leads straight with the prediction at hero typography. Line spacing widens on the more urgent surfaces so multi-clause predictions stay readable when they wrap.

Removing a license from this Mac and swapping in a new key now both prompt with clear consequences. The deactivate dialog explains the activation slot returns to your pool. Activating a new key when one is already on the Mac warns that the existing license stays put if the new one fails or you cancel — no silent overwrite.

First-run calendar guard surface gained a one-line hint pointing at the master switch up top, so the empty state doesn't read as broken before you've enabled monitoring.

item.title: Version 1.2.5
item.description:
1.2.5

Per-app energy chart and ranking, fixed.

The 24-hour and 7-day per-app charts now downsample. Previously every 5-minute sample landed as its own point, so the curve was a fuzzy band on the day view (≈288 points) and visual noise on the week view (≈2016 points). Buckets are anchored to the chart's visible window — 24h collapses to ~30-minute averages, 7d to ~3-hour averages — and a freshly-installed app with only 30 minutes of samples now occupies one bucket at the right time position instead of stacking five dots on top of each other at the right edge. The 1-hour view stays raw. PointMarks removed from the per-app chart; the line alone reads cleanly.

Row ordering matches the displayed number. The top-apps list now sorts by estimated battery percent — the value actually printed under each app name — instead of the per-sample energy impact score. Previously a row reading "238% in the last 7 days" could appear below a row reading "34%" because their internal impact scores ran the other way. On Intel Macs (no battery attribution), the ranking falls back to energy impact as before.

24-hour and 7-day views now exclude apps that weren't observed for most of the window. An app whose earliest sample lands more than 10% into the window — 2.4h on the day view, 16.8h on the week view — was either recently installed or only started running late, and its battery share isn't comparable to apps that ran the whole time. The 1-hour view keeps all apps visible so fresh-launch UX still has something to show on the first tick.

item.title: Version 1.2.6
item.description:
1.2.6

Calmer home, quieter window chrome, redesigned rescue receipt.

The Pro / Trial home badge dropped its card chrome. The licensed and trial states now sit as an inline strip with just the Pro pill on the left and the Manage link on the right, no box around them. Previous attempts to match the box to the hero card below kept reading as slightly misaligned — narrower, wider, or floating on a different plane. As a top utility strip the row stops competing with the hero card directly underneath.

Card surfaces are now fully opaque. Light and dark themes both used to render cards at 94–98% opacity, which let the window-wide washi parchment patina bleed through onto card backgrounds. The intent was a subtle paper texture; the effect was the background overlapping the cards. Cards now have a clean ground; the washi texture stays visible in the gutters between cards where it belongs.

The window's top chrome strip no longer leaves a visible seam. The old mask held full opacity for the first half then ramped to clear, which produced a faint horizontal line across the window — and the macOS rounded window corners pinched that line asymmetrically, making the corners look broken. A pure linear falloff dissolves the chrome into the parchment with no detectable boundary.

The Battery Rescue Receipt sheet got the full zen pass:

  • A hanko stamp glyph (concentric hinomaru rings around a checkmark seal) replaces the bolt-heart-in-warning-circle. Reads as stamped / approved, matches the receipt metaphor.
  • A 印 ("seal") kanji watermark sits at top-trailing at paper-faint opacity, matching the watermark pattern used on the rest of the saga cards.
  • The receipt body sits in an inner tinted-and-bordered panel so the summary reads as the stamped content of the receipt, not another paragraph on the card. A hairline washi divider separates the header from the body like a tear line.
  • The outer card gained the saga card vocabulary — ZenRadius.xl, theme border stroke, soft shadow — so the sheet sits at the same elevation as its neighbours instead of looking like a flat sub-element.
  • All three actions now lead with icons: Copy (filled doc), Share (system arrow-up-square), Not Now (xmark). The dismiss option previously read as inert text; with the same icon-leading vocabulary as its peers it reads as a peer control, just visually subordinate.
  • Hover scale lift added to every button.

item.title: Version 1.2.7
item.description:
1.2.7

Rescue receipt redesigned, copy quieted.

The Battery Rescue Receipt sheet got the full zen pass. A hanko stamp glyph — concentric hinomaru rings around a checkmark seal — replaces the bolt-heart-in-warning-circle hero. A 印 ("seal") kanji sits as a paper-faint watermark in the top corner. The receipt body now reads as a real receipt: two stat tiles for the saved-at percentage and the time-remaining estimate, then a hinomaru-tinted outcome strip below them — the equivalent of a "PAID" stamp on paper. A hairline washi divider separates the header from the body like a tear line.

The Not Now button stopped looking like inert text. It's now a real bordered button with the same icon-leading vocabulary as Copy and Share (xmark glyph), an inline "Esc" keycap so the keyboard shortcut is discoverable on the surface itself, and Esc actually dismisses the sheet now via the standard cancel-action binding.

The copy across every language stepped away from the marketing-deck register. "Sensei intervention: successful. Copy or share the receipt when the save is too dramatic to keep private." became "A small moment worth keeping. Copy or share if you'd like." The receipt summary dropped its redundant "intervention: successful" tail. The outcome strip carries a single word — "Saved." in English, "Gerettet." in German, "A salvo." in Spanish, "Sauvé." in French, "救えた。" in Japanese — beside the seal stamp. Title shortened in English and German ("Rescue Receipt", "Rettungsbeleg") so it doesn't repeat "Battery". The kicker above the title carries the rescue timestamp now ("印 · 28 May 14:20"), not a duplicate of the title in caps.

Stat tile labels swapped from "BATTERY" / "RUNWAY" to "Low" / "Left" — sentence case, less business-card.

item.title: Version 1.2.8
item.description:
1.2.8

Menu polish, meeting forecast in the menu, redesigned Battery Health.

The menu-bar dropdown got context-aware about the time-remaining line. When a charge limit is set, it now reads "1h 45m until 85%" instead of the bare "1h 45m"; the now-redundant "Charging to 85%" segment drops out so the line stops repeating itself. On battery it reads "1h 45m left"; without a limit it reads "1h 45m until full". The lightning bolt next to the line is now a template image, so it tints white on dark menus and black on light menus the same way macOS's own menu glyphs do. The Pro badge in the menu header lifts ~2pt above the title baseline so it reads as a superscript flourish instead of hanging off the bottom.

A new meeting-forecast row sits directly below the status line whenever Calendar Battery Guard is enabled. Layout is [icon] Accent · body text at 10pt — the accent label is the only thing that picks up a colour. Severity → accent:

  • comfortable → green "Clear"
  • tight → orange "Tight"
  • critical → red "Charge"
  • catastrophic → red "Charge now"

Icon matches the accent (calendar.badge.checkmark / .clock / .exclamationmark). Body text stays in labelColor (white on dark, black on light) so the row doesn't saturate. When the guard is on but nothing's pending in the lookahead window, the row shows a green "Clear · No meetings in next 4h" confirmation. When the guard is off, the row hides entirely.

The Top Power-Hungry Apps panel gained a small info-circle next to its subtitle on the 24-hour and 7-day windows. On hover the system tooltip explains the coverage filter — "Only apps observed for most of the last 24 hours appear here, so percentages stay comparable across rows." The 1-hour view stays badge-less.

Battery Health got a full redesign. Each of the four tiles now leads with a tinted glyph in a soft tinted disc and stacks the value + kicker label beside it. Each metric carries its own colour band:

  • Capacity: green ≥85%, kin (gold) 75–84%, hinomaru <75%. Inline 3pt rail visualises 0–100%.
  • Cycles: neutral 0–600, kin 600–899, hinomaru ≥900 (against Apple's ~1000-cycle design target).
  • Temperature: aizome blue <10°C, neutral 10–34°C, kin 35–39°C, hinomaru ≥40°C.
  • Condition: green "Normal", hinomaru "Service" — the verdict text itself picks up the tint so the row reads at a glance.

Narrow layouts collapse to a 2×2 grid instead of a single column so the tiles keep a comfortable reading width.

The BATTERY · SENSEI title chrome stopped being translucent. The strip previously used .ultraThinMaterial, which let the hero card and parchment patina bleed through even at full opacity. The top of the chrome is now a solid theme fill — only the lower ~40% fades into the parchment below, so the title region no longer overlaps the content underneath it.

Marketing 1.2.7 → 1.2.8, build 48 → 49.
